text: Hi! Welcome to our ribbon plaza. Let's count Catalan numbers, and watch the equations make each new value.
A ribbon can go up and down. It starts on this line, finishes on the line, and never goes below it.
One up step and one down step make a pair. Catalan numbers count the different paths for each number of pairs.
With no pairs, there is one empty path. An empty path still counts as one choice. Our first value is one.
The small label tells us the number of pairs. The big number tells us how many paths. They tell us different things.
We will count from C zero to C thirty. First we will see the paths, then a quicker equation will make the growing values.
To move one place forward, take the last value, multiply by four times the new label minus two, then divide by the new label plus one.
Always multiply first. The middle window shows the whole product. Then divide that product into equal shares. One share gives the next Catalan number.
These number windows show values. The ribbons point to the calculation; they are not a picture of every path when the numbers become large.
one times two, divided by two, equals.
We have one and one. The first belongs to no pairs; the second belongs to one pair. Same value, different places. Keep both.
For one pair, the only path goes up, then down. Its two ends touch the line. There is exactly one way.
one times six, divided by three, equals.
For two pairs, we can climb twice and come down twice, or make two little peaks. Different paths, the same number of pairs.
two times ten, divided by four, equals.
Here are all five paths for three pairs. Watch the first step up. Follow its matching step down: that is the first return to the line.
Inside this first arch is a smaller path. After the arch is another path. Choose the inside and the part after it, then join them.
If the inside has no pairs, the part after has two. One choice times two choices gives two paths. Both belong in this first group.
One pair inside and one after gives one times one: one path. Two pairs inside and none after gives two times one: two paths.
Add the three groups: two plus one plus two makes five. Each path has only one first return, so every path appears once.
five times fourteen, divided by five, equals.
Look back at our equation. Five times fourteen made seventy. Dividing seventy into five equal shares gave fourteen in each share. Nothing was rounded.
The path rule and this arithmetic rule give the same Catalan numbers. We can follow the small paths, and use exact arithmetic as the values grow.

From one empty path to a very big number, every place had its own value. Thanks for counting Catalan numbers with me. See you next time!
